extracted.intended_audience: scholars/editors of early-modern English literature; textual editors and bibliographers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and editorial practice for producing a critical edition of early-modern texts (textual variants, notes, apparatus, indexes, and selection of extracts). Aimed at editors preparing annotated editions and bibliographic apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and report textual variants / MS readings
rubrics_metrics.description: The variations between the printed copy and Dr. Bright's MS. are so considerable, that the latter text is here given entire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When manuscript (MS) readings differ substantially from printed editions, present the MS text in full or clearly record variant readings and transpositions; indicate MS vs. printed numbering (e.g., MS. no. vs Bliss no.) and give the precise places of changes. Note transpositions, omissions, or slight changes explicitly so readers can compare texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concise, instructive notes (without prolixity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notes are instructive without prolixity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotations should clarify meanings, citations, and contexts while avoiding excessive length. Use notes to illuminate obscure terms, point to sources, and supply brief commentary and cross-references rather than long essays in every footnote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a useful, comprehensive index
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-constructed index helps readers locate material and greatly increases a work's utility. Include entries for characters, key terms, variant readings, and documented sources; cross-reference where appropriate. Provide a table of editions or an editions list to complement the index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix with black-letter / documentary information
rubrics_metrics.description: The appendix contains an ample store of black-letter information, and will introduce almost every reader to some new acquaintances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an appendix collecting facsimile material, contemporary pamphlets, advertisements, black-letter documents, and other archival items that contextualize the edition. The appendix should be substantial enough to supply primary-source background not reproduced in the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document edition history and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: See references to tables of editions (e.g., 'a table of the editions is given') and preservation/alteration of title-leaves and notes on ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record edition history (dates, variant editions, augmentations), collational information, provenance (ownership marks, pasted slips, annotated copies), and any changes to title-pages or headings. Note when an editor's description of editions is later corrected by additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide illustrative quotations and cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes and illustrations (quotations) from other works are used to illustrate characters and terms (e.g., quotations from plays to explain words/phrases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support readings and character explanations with contemporary quotations and examples from related works; cross-reference similar usages and cite sources (play title, date, page) so readers can verify contexts. Use such illustrations sparingly to illuminate sense and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and present extracts when full texts are excessively long
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two very long letters ... --too long to quote in full--from which I have thought it worth while to make extracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documentary items (e.g., long letters) are too lengthy for full reproduction, provide well-chosen extracts that preserve key content and context, and indicate the existence, date, and location of the full text (manuscript shelfmark) so interested readers can consult the complete item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate emendations and correct obvious textual errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples in the notes: 'For "ballast" read "last blast"' and other corrective readings are supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where original texts contain clear errors, supply suggested emendations and mark them in the apparatus or footnotes. Distinguish conjectural corrections from documentary readings, and provide justification or source evidence for emendations.
